statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-11979: in the xmlcatalog utility's --shell mode, usershell() copies each input line into fixed-size stack buffers (command[100], arg[400], argv[20]) without bounds checks, so an overly long line overflows them: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/work_items/1124. Upstream added the bounds checks in commit https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/c2e233fc1b341685fc99621b2768b503f777a72e on master and its 2.15 branch backport https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/cd48d441f8fb1cf84e74c393310b72e4534de435, released in libxml2 2.15.4; the change is in xmlcatalog.c, which now rejects an overlong command or argument and too many arguments with the messages "Invalid command", "Invalid arg" and "Too much arguments", plus a test. Debian rates it unimportant and has not fixed it in trixie: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-11979. The DHI libxml2 packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of libxml2 2.13.9; DHI backports the upstream xmlcatalog.c change onto it. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (main and security, x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source libxml2 at 2.13.9-r0, 2.13.9-r1, 2.13.9-r2 and 2.13.9-r3. We checked every one of them, each verified against its index checksum. The xmlcatalog program in the libxml2-utils package of 2.13.9-r3 contains all three messages the fix adds, on both architectures, and its usershell() function in the libxml2-dbg debug symbols is larger than in earlier builds (1500 bytes against 1399 on x86_64, 1616 against 1540 on aarch64). In 2.13.9-r0, 2.13.9-r1 and 2.13.9-r2 xmlcatalog has none of the three messages, on either architecture. No other package of these builds ships the xmlcatalog program (libxml2-doc carries only its documentation), and no other ELF file in them has a usershell() symbol. The range ends at 2.13.9-r3, the first published build with the fix.

The DHI libxml2 packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie libxml2 with the upstream xmlcatalog.c change backported. The DHI Debian repository now publishes one build from source libxml2, a rebuild of Debian's 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3, for amd64 and arm64. We checked every binary package of it, each verified against its index checksum: the xmlcatalog program in libxml2-utils contains all three messages the fix adds on both architectures. Earlier rebuilds are no longer in the repository, so they could not be checked and read as affected. The range ends at that rebuild, the lowest published build, which carries the fix.
